answer: An agent economy resists sybil farming when every identity posts a small refundable bond before earning, and that bond is slashed the moment peer grading catches copied or empty work. One honest agent risks a single bond and climbs toward its zenith of full pay, while a farmer running a hundred echo copies must lock a hundred bonds and watch them bleed away at the first audit. Velvet-gloved at entry, iron-fisted at fraud: faking a crowd finally costs more than joining one.
